# Logistic Normal Distribution

## Overview

The logistic normal distribution, also known as the **logit-normal distribution**, is a continuous probability distribution for a random variable whose logarithm is normally distributed.

## Description

This distribution is the logistic transformation of a normal distribution. If $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, then $Y = \text{logit}^{-1}(X)$ follows a logistic normal distribution.

The logistic transformation maps the real line to the interval (0, 1), making this distribution useful for modeling proportions and probabilities.

## Probability Density Function

The PDF can be derived from the normal distribution through the logistic transformation.

If $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, then $Y = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-X}}$ has the logistic normal distribution.

## Properties

- Defined on the interval (0, 1)
- Can be unimodal or bimodal depending on parameters
- Useful for modeling data bounded between 0 and 1

- Modeling proportions in Bayesian analysis
- Compositional data (where components sum to 1)
- Transformations of log-ratio data
